title: Air Manila 702
summary: Air Manila Flight 702, a Lockheed L-188A Electra, crashed during takeoff from NAS Agana, Guam. Seconds after lifting off, the No. 3 engine propeller feathered. The captain continued the takeoff despite not yet reaching VR speed, when company policy required immediate abort. The aircraft reached only 75-100 feet altitude, lost climb capability after flaps were retracted too low, struck rising terrain and crashed, killing all 46 on board plus one person on the ground.
probable_cause: The probable cause of this accident was the loss of climb capability after the crew retracted the flaps at too low an altitude to clear the rising terrain. The flaps were retracted after the No. 3 propeller feathered as the aircraft lifted off the runway. Contributing to the accident was the captain's decision to continue the takeoff after an engine failed before reaching rotation speed. (p. 21)

factors.evidence: Seconds after lifting off from the runway, the No. 3 propeller feathered during or just after liftoff. (p. 6)
The captain continued the takeoff after an engine failed before reaching rotation speed, when there was adequate runway available to have aborted. (p. 20)
The crew retracted landing gear and flaps before the aircraft reached the apex of the climb at an altitude where the flaps-up climb performance was insufficient. (p. 21)

Aircraft was not accelerated to a speed at which a climb could be maintained in a flaps-up configuration; aircraft rotated to a nose-high attitude with resultant loss of airspeed and lateral stability. (p. 21)
Aircraft struck terrain in tail-low attitude, dragged across ground for 220 feet, crossed a highway striking an automobile, and burst into flames. (p. 6)

events.text: Air Manila Flight 702 initiated rolling takeoff from runway 6L at Naval Air Station Agana.
Aircraft lifted off between 6,600 and 8,000 feet down runway, with liftoff estimated at 7,500-foot point. Most witnesses stated attitude at liftoff was normal.
No. 3 propeller feathered during or just after liftoff, as aircraft was beginning initial climb phase. Witness heard definite change in propeller sound from high rpm to low rpm and back to high rpm.
Captain continued takeoff after engine failure despite not yet having reached VR speed, when adequate runway was available for abort and company policy required immediate abort.
Crew retracted landing gear and flaps before aircraft reached apex of climb at altitude of approximately 75-100 feet, before airspeed was adequate for flaps-up climb configuration.
Aircraft was not accelerated to speed at which climb could be maintained in flaps-up configuration. Aircraft yawed to the right, then rotated to nose-high attitude.
Aircraft in tail-low attitude began descending toward terrain. Slow acceleration had resulted in excessive runway usage for takeoff, and aircraft reached only 75-100 feet altitude.

Aircraft struck rising terrain approximately 4,300 feet beyond end of runway 6L. Aft fuselage dragged along ground for 220 feet in right-wing-down attitude, then crashed through chain-link perimeter fence, crossed highway striking automobile (driver killed), and burst into flames in vacant area 4,900 feet from runway end.
